qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Dermatological healthcare portfolio (Cetaphil) and aesthetic injectables (Restylane, Dysport, Sculptra) backed by injector relationships, but capital efficiency is structurally diluted by ~$9.8B in goodwill/intangibles from the 2019 private equity buyout. Historical 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~5.0% (FY25 ~7.8%), far below the 12% hurdle, while aesthetic injectables face intense cyclicality and price competition from AbbVie/Allergan, Evolus, and emerging biosimilars.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (3b = N, REJECT). Pure-play dermatology and aesthetic injectables provider structurally burdened by $9.8B in goodwill/intangibles from 2019 buyout. 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 5.0% (FY25 ~7.8%) fails the 12% minimum hurdle, alongside fierce competition in neuromodulators and fillers.
qualitative.evidence: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 5.03% (2022: negative, 2023: 4.7%, 2024: 5.0%, 2025: 7.8%). Balance sheet carries $2.58B long-term debt and $9.77B of goodwill/intangibles against $8.15B book equity. While Nemluvio launch and cash generation improved in 2025 ($967M owner FCF), capital base remains unproven across a full public cycle and returns on capital fail the Munger hurdle.
